gaps.sentence: 'I have to catch the last train,' she said. She said she ___ catch the last train.
gaps.explanation: Have to (obligation) backshifts to had to after a past reporting verb.

gaps.sentence: They ___ us that the museum had closed early.
gaps.explanation: Tell somebody (that)... — 'told' needs the direct personal object 'us'; 'said' cannot take it.

gaps.sentence: 'I will always love you,' he whispered. He whispered that he ___ always love me.
gaps.explanation: Will backshifts to would; 'you' shifts to 'me' from the speaker's new perspective.

gaps.sentence: 'Where are you going?' she asked her brother. She asked her brother where he ___ going.
gaps.explanation: are you going → he was going: statement order with backshifted continuous.

gaps.sentence: 'Someone has stolen my bike,' he cried. He cried that someone ___ his bike.
gaps.explanation: have stolen backshifts to had stolen after the past reporting verb 'cried'.

gaps.sentence: 'I'm meeting them tomorrow evening,' she said. She said she was meeting them ___ evening.
gaps.explanation: Tomorrow evening becomes the next (or the following) evening.

gaps.sentence: 'I'll pay for the damage,' he said. He ___ pay for the damage.
gaps.explanation: 'I'll pay' as a voluntary act is reported with 'offered to pay'.

gaps.sentence: 'You should get a second opinion,' the doctor said. The doctor ___ a second opinion.
gaps.explanation: 'Advise' is the reporting verb that takes object + to-infinitive; suggest and offer do not.
